KEY MESSAGE 1... High pressure continues to keep enough dry air
in place and subsidence aloft to preclude a rain threat through
Saturday outside maybe a stray, short lived seabreeze shower. 
In fact, the 7/31 00Z KMHX sounding had PWATs of around 1", 
which is climatologically near the 10th percentile for the time 
of the year. Light winds and seasonable temps again today, with 
light westerly winds become southerly behind the sea breeze. 
Temps near 90s inland, mid 80s along the coast. High gradually 
shifts offshore tonight, with the return of synoptically 
southerly flow Saturday. With the onshore flow, atmospheric 
profile gradually moistens, but given how dry we are the 
moisture will not rebound fast enough for an appreciable rain 
chance Saturday. Despite the low chances for rain Saturday, we 
should see an increase in cloud cover, which will keep temps 
Saturday similar to today (near 90 inland, mid 80s along the 
coast) despite the southerly flow. 

Despite the calm winds and mostly clear skies paired with recent
rainfall, the subsidence should be strong enough to prevent
impactful fog formation this morning and Saturday morning.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Sunday morning an upper trough will be deepening
over the Ohio Valley as it moves towards the eastern seaboard,
while at the surface an associated closed low is expected to 
traverse the Great Lakes region. As these features move east,
they will encounter the Bermuda high and the upper trough over
the Ohio Valley is expected to stall before reaching the 
eastern seaboard. While the main trough stalls, embedded 
shortwaves rounding the base of the trough may advect into the 
region Sunday through at least Monday. These features, in 
addition to the sea breeze each afternoon/evening, will be the 
main forcing present for a notable increase in precip chances. 


Sunday morning the warm front will be moving through, with maybe
some more stratiform along it and dewpoints increasing behind 
it. As the day progresses and the profile moistens, the 
environment becomes more favorable for more robust convection to
occur. In the afternoon/evening hours, we could see enough 
recovery paired with forcing aloft for showers and 
thunderstorms. Cloud cover will play a big role in how large 
CAPEs can truly get, but with the dewpoints rising there should 
be enough instability entering the region for CAPE values of 
1000-2000 J/kg Sunday. While shear is not too impressive with 
the unidirectional SE flow, the combination of long, skinny 
CAPEs, PWATs over 2", and slow storm motions could result in 
heavy rainfall rates. where storms develop. Precip coverage 
Sunday is expected to be more scattered in nature with two foci
for convection. First is along the coast where showers can tap 
into Gulf Stream instability throughout the day along and behind
the warm front, and second is in the afternoon/evening hours 
along the Coastal Plain west of hwy 17 where forcing is a bit 
better thanks to closer proximity to the trough. 

Monday the trough is still stalled to our west, but is just a
little bit closer allowing for weak height falls and weak
embedded shortwaves to move through aloft. This better forcing,
paired with another day of long skinny CAPEs and PWATs north of
2" brings high precip chances with heavy rainfall rates and slow
storm motion vectors. The better forcing likely brings with it 
better coverage of precip. All this brings flash flooding
concerns to mind, especially with how much rain has been
observed in many locations in the past 1-2 weeks. We are
currently in a Marginal (level 1/5) Excessive Rain Outlook for
Sunday. What prevents it from being higher is likely the
uncertainty on instability with antecedent cloud cover and the
lack of substantial ground-level forcing. With high temps
forecast to only be in the low to mid 80s Sunday, the sea 
breeze may be weak in nature. 

Beyond Monday, the trough/low is still expected to linger to our
west until eventually it gets picked up and shifted to our north 
by another trough moving through the Great Lakes region. As a
result, daily elevated precip chances continue through mid-week.
